newsitem.title: ZAMBIA: Cyprus Amax to spend $300 mln on Zambia mine.
newsitem.headline: Cyprus Amax to spend $300 mln on Zambia mine.

text.p: Cyprus Amax Minerals Company is expected to spend up to $300 million in developing Zambia's Kansanshi copper mine after feasibility studies, mines minister Christon Tembo said on Monday.
"We believe that, should the pre-feasibility and feasibility studies by Cyprus prove positive, between $200 to $300 million will need to be spent in developing the mine," Tembo told Reuters.
Kansanshi was the first ZCCM mine to be sold under Zambia's ambitious privatisation of state assets.
U.S. based-Cyprus Amax agreed with the Zambian government in January to acquire 80 percent of Kansanshi mine and said it would spend at least $20 million on exploration and feasibility studies.
Zambia Consolidated Copper Mine (ZCCM) retains a 20 percent carried interest in the mine.
Kansanshi has a resource base of 24.4 million tonnes of ore at 2.9 percent copper content and is being mined at a small scale.
Cyprus Amax will pay Zambia Consolidated Copper Mines (ZCCM) a total of $28 million for the mine.
Tembo said negotiations for the sale of other ZCCM assets, including Konkola Deep and Konkola North, are expected to be completed shortly.
"The Konkola North project has been offered for development to Anglovaal of South Africa and an option agreement is to be signed soon," Tembo said.
The minister said the government also expected a memorandum of understanding with a consortium led by Anglo American Corp of South Africa on the development of the Konkola Deep mining project.
